scope: Only trial==2 records, with trial1 used solely for identity consistency and descriptive throughput ratios. No conclusions about round3.

expected_reference.reason: Declared ineligible memory store; seeded SQLite file remains unchanged, so database_valid=false is expected and not eligible for SQLite ranking.

evidence_limits: Server resource limits and seccomp are inspected per trial. Load image and CPU/memory limits are recorded in environment-bench.json and enforced by controller Docker arguments; per-trial load-container inspection is not retained.
HTTP non-2xx/3xx and socket counters are separate observations, with no assumed distinct-failure count. Individual status codes, response bodies and per-route breakdowns were not captured.
CPU is summed live self plus waited-child CPU over the sampled interval. RSS is summed service-process RSS after load, not peak/container memory; shared pages may be counted more than once.
Post-growth includes warmup writes; positive growth and SQLite quick_check do not establish per-request durability or absence of transient SQL errors.
Native image architecture is enforced by the controller image inspection; this audit did not inspect removed containers or run additional workloads.

crossround_drift_screen.purpose: Descriptive broad-system-drift screen only; individual variation is expected and no statistical significance is inferred.
crossround_drift_screen.interpretation: No broad common directional shift is apparent from these ratios. Individual changes are large in some cases; two rounds cannot establish significance or exclude time-varying host effects. Ratios do not change inclusion or ranking rules.

independent_cross_check.scope: Read-only independent check of the same 100 trial-2 records and paired throughput ratios.
checks: Raw wrk counts, durations, displayed RPS, HTTP/socket counters and percentile conversions/order
CPU delta/self/waited-child/process sums and RSS conversion/process sums
Paired descriptive throughput ratios and absence of an obvious shared directional drift
